title: Optimizing Real-Time Edge Vision Pipelines
business: Retail analytics firms deploying computer vision models on local NVIDIA hardware to track inventory.
problem: Standard deep learning frameworks often suffer from high latency and inconsistent throughput when running complex vision models on edge devices, leading to missed inventory updates.
solution: NVIDIA TensorRT optimizes trained models by compiling them into engines tailored for specific NVIDIA GPU configurations, enabling efficient inference through layer fusion and precision calibration.
steps: Export the trained vision model to the ONNX format.
Use the trtexec tool to compile the ONNX model into a hardware-specific TensorRT engine.
Configure the builder to utilize mixed precision (e.g., FP16) to reduce memory footprint.
Load the optimized engine into the production inference application using the TensorRT runtime.
outcome: Achieving consistent, low-latency inference performance that allows for real-time inventory tracking without hardware upgrades.
limitation: TensorRT engines are hardware-specific; if the underlying GPU architecture changes, the engine must be rebuilt for the new target device, which can be verified by checking the engine compatibility metadata.

import tensorrt as trt
# Load the logger for engine building
logger = trt.Logger(trt.Logger.WARNING)
# Create a builder instance
builder = trt.Builder(logger)
# Define network and build engine from ONNX
network = builder.create_network(1 << int(trt.NetworkDefinitionCreationFlag.EXPLICIT_BATCH))
# ... parser logic to populate network ...
engine = builder.build_serialized_network(network, config) # Compile to optimized engine

By automatically upgrading the physical GPU hardware to a newer generation.
By bypassing the need for trained models and generating new weights at runtime.
By converting all models to a generic CPU-compatible format for faster execution.
